title: Using Java Documentation and Learning Resources
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of using java documentation and learning resources and identify when it is appropriate in a Java program.
Apply at least one of the lesson topics—official java learning tutorials—in a small, readable example.
Predict the example result and check it against the stated output or a boundary-case test.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will study using java documentation and learning resources with a short explanation, an original visual map, a Java example, and a check you can perform yourself. Focus on the relationship between the rule and the behavior rather than memorizing isolated syntax.
content.why_it_matters: This concept matters because it helps you make sure your terminal and editor use the JDK you intend to learn and build with. In this lesson, focus on official java learning tutorials and use a minimal example to check what the rule actually guarantees.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: A setup is correct only when the selected runtime and compiler match the intended JDK. Check `java -version` and `javac -version` separately, and verify PATH/JAVA_HOME rather than guessing which installation is active. Apply that reasoning specifically to official java learning tutorials and confirm the result with the example or a targeted test. The important habit is to make the assumptions explicit and use the code example as a small experiment.

content_blocks.title: How the pieces fit
content_blocks.text: Connect official java learning tutorials with java api documentation before choosing an implementation. The example is a small, observable case; extend it by changing one input and checking a boundary, invalid value, or compatibility limit where relevant.

content_blocks.run_instructions: Relate the JDK tools to the source-to-program workflow. For ordinary Java SE examples, use JDK 25, save a complete class as Main.java, and run `javac Main.java` followed by `java Main`. CodeLeaf does not execute Java in the browser; use a local JDK for these examples. Preview-only and configuration-file examples have their own version or filename notes.
content_blocks.reset_steps: Restore the original example, remove any temporary output files it created, and rerun the baseline case. Do not leave credentials, generated private data, or large test files in the project directory.

content_blocks.title: Professional habit
content_blocks.text: Keep one clear hypothesis per experiment. Check the version, read the error message, test boundaries, and record what evidence supports your conclusion.

content.task: Try it yourself: verify your local JDK and editor setup for using java documentation and learning resources. Record the relevant command output, then explain what each result proves. Do not change global environment settings until you know which JDK your terminal is using.

common_mistakes.problem: Applying the rule from memory without checking its exact contract.
common_mistakes.why: Small differences in type, scope, API version, or input shape can change the result.
common_mistakes.fix: Inspect the relevant official API/language documentation and build a minimal reproducer.

common_mistakes.problem: Testing only a single happy path.
common_mistakes.why: Boundary values and failures often reveal assumptions hidden by the simplest example.
common_mistakes.fix: Add an empty, boundary, or invalid case and state the expected behavior before running it.

common_mistakes.why: It becomes difficult to identify the actual cause of a different result.
common_mistakes.fix: Change one factor at a time and keep a short record of observed behavior.
